EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a coherent set of bands that are typical for an organophosphate ester containing a C=O group.  Key matches are: (a) a strong ν(C=O) at 1723 cm⁻¹, compatible with the ketone/ester carbonyl present only in candidate 1; (b) a group of phosphate-related bands – ν(P=O) / ν(PO₂) asymmetric at 1235–1192 cm⁻¹, ν(PO–C) at 1087 cm⁻¹, ν(PO₃) symmetric at 974 cm⁻¹, and P–O–C / P–C deformation near 816, 619 and 585 cm⁻¹ – matching the expected fingerprint of a dialkyl phosphonate; (c) strong C–H stretches at 2932 cm⁻¹ and CH bending at 1441 cm⁻¹, consistent with the isopropyl groups in candidate 1. None of the other candidates contain a phosphoryl (P=O) group capable of generating the full 1235/1190/1087/974/816 cm⁻¹ pattern, and some lack a 1720 cm⁻¹ carbonyl. Therefore, candidate 1 (CC(C)OP(=O)(OC(C)C)C(C=O)=NO) best accounts for the observed Raman peaks.
